argument: CEEMEA seat has no genuine transmission channel into this pair — long PEP / short RSPS is a US single-name idiosyncratic structure that isolates exactly the exposure my mandate exists to price. Three observations, none disqualifying. (1) Pair construction is macro-clean: the RSPS short neutralizes the US staples factor, and the residual that remains is PEP-specific (Frito-Lay volume trajectory, international snacks/beverage mix), so EM beta, DXY, and US rates are second-order. No factor-cap concern from my side. (2) The one channel worth naming: PEP carries meaningful EM/international revenue exposure (Mexico, Turkey, Poland/Central Europe bottling and snacks) relative to the equal-weight staples basket. My framework flags CEEMEA consumer purchasing power as soft — CEE wage growth is decelerating off the 2024-25 peak, and EM FX carry-adjusted depreciation remains a translation drag for US staples reporters. That is a mild headwind to PEP's international organic line vs. a domestic-weighted RSPS, but it is fully consistent with — not contradictory to — the affordability-led volume thesis, which is primarily a North America Frito-Lay story. I treat it as noise inside the stated stop_ratio of 4.35. (3) On the originator's own key risk #4 (valuations feed rate-limited, multiples leg unverified): I second that as the weakest link. A 4th-percentile pair ratio plus 4.3% yield is a valuation-anchored argument at its core, and the multiples cross-check is exactly the leg that would confirm or kill 'cheap with a catalyst' vs. 'cheap and de-rating' — my occupational bias list exists precisely for that distinction. Recommend the multiples check complete before this advances past debate.
